summary: Legacy Django 1.11-era app with embedded project and app code. Multiple production secrets are hardcoded (Django SECRET_KEY and a Dialogflow client access token), DEBUG is enabled, and CORS/ALLOWED_HOSTS are development-oriented. Dependencies are very old and tightly pinned (Django 1.11.5 only), which is EOL and contains known CVEs; modernization to a supported Django/Python will require non-trivial refactoring (middleware settings, urlresolvers, admin/configs, tests). Dependency audit failed due to install/build issues with an old dialogflow-lite dependency, indicating fragility. CI targets Python 2.7/3.4/3.5 via Travis (defunct), and there are model code defects (duplicate created_at field) and minor packaging inconsistencies (license mismatch). Overall, high risk to take on without conditions; expect significant time to update, secure, and stabilize before feature work.

red_flags.title: Hardcoded Dialogflow client access token committed to repo
EOL Django version tightly pinned (blocks security updates)
Use of deprecated django.core.urlresolvers (breaks on modern Django)
Model defect: Response.created_at defined twice (field overwritten)
Outdated CI targets unsupported Python versions; Travis CI config present
License inconsistency between setup metadata and classifiers

clarifying_questions: What Python and Django versions must we support in production? Is a modernization to a supported Django LTS (e.g., 3.2/4.2/5.x) acceptable as part of scope?
Are the committed Dialogflow client_access_token and Django SECRET_KEY real/active? If so, can we rotate them immediately and move secrets to environment variables?
Do you want to continue using dialogflow-lite, or can we migrate to the official Dialogflow client library and API v2+?
What hosting environment are we targeting (OS, Python runtime, DB)? Any constraints on using Docker/containers to isolate legacy dependencies?
Is it acceptable to replace the Travis CI setup with a modern CI (GitHub Actions) and to drop Python 2.7/3.4/3.5 support?
What are your priorities: stabilizing and securing the current app, upgrading stack, or adding new features?
Are there any integration requirements (CORS origins, ALLOWED_HOSTS, domain names) we should lock down for production?
Do you have existing Dialogflow agent configuration and required scopes/keys, and can you provide non-production credentials for development?
Do you need database migrations/data preservation, and is it acceptable to adjust models (fix duplicate fields) as part of the upgrade?
Any test coverage or performance requirements we should target post-upgrade?
rationale: High security exposure from committed secrets and DEBUG on; EOL Django and legacy patterns imply notable refactor to reach supported, secure runtime. Dependencies are fragile/outdated and CI is obsolete. Work is feasible but requires a defined upgrade/security-hardening phase before feature delivery. Proceed only if scope includes rotating secrets, removing hardcoded credentials, updating dependencies, and agreeing on a modernization path.
